quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: At a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Let other traffic pass if they are close enough to cause a crash.
Only yield to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic pass if they are close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, let traffic in the lanes you want to enter go first. Be ready to stop, but you can go if no other traffic is coming.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other cars?

options.text: No. Driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes. It is good defensive driving.
Yes. It is always safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. Driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive too slowly and block normal traffic flow, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: When is it legal to drive faster than the speed limit?

options.text: Never.
If it seems safe and reasonable.
When you are passing another car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Always follow the posted speed limit. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but never faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A downhill or steep hill is coming.
Road work is ahead.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: A downhill or steep hill is coming.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you about a steep or long downhill section. The hill may have sharp turns.

questions.question: You are exiting the freeway on a curved downhill ramp. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before a curve. You cannot see far ahead, and braking in a curve can cause your car to skid.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: Construction is ahead.
No one can pass.
Anyone can pass if safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anyone can pass if safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass?

options.text: When the car ahead moves to the right.
When the yellow line on your side is broken.
When the yellow line on the other side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line on your side is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if it is safe. Check the line next to your side of the road.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a construction zone?

options.text: Speed up a little.
Be ready for anything unexpected.
Workers will move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones are unpredictable. Drive carefully to protect yourself, other drivers, and workers.

questions.question: How do you prevent hydroplaning when it rains?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep your speed steady.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on water instead of the road. Slowing down in rain reduces this risk. Driving too fast makes your tires lose grip on the road.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring straight ahead at the road.
Looking in your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Looking in your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every two to five seconds to stay aware of hazards. Do not stare only ahead. In fog, use low beam lights, not high beams.

questions.question: What should a driver do when approaching a broken traffic light?

options.text: Stop completely and let others go first before entering the intersection.
You do not need to stop if the intersection looks empty.
Drive fast through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and let others go first before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Always come to a complete stop. Look both ways and yield to others before entering the intersection.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels and makes you lose steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels and makes you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock your front wheels. This causes you to lose the ability to steer. Slow down before you reach icy areas to avoid needing hard braking.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ends ahead.
You must choose to go either right or left.
A four-way intersection is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must choose to go either right or left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that the road splits into two directions. You must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: Which of the following is not safe on the highway?

options.text: Slower traffic stays in the right lane.
Change lanes without using a signal.
If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without using a signal.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Keep to the right lane if you are going slower than other traffic. Do not back up or turn around on a highway. If you miss your exit, continue to the next exit.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may go if:

options.text: You first come to a complete stop.
You wait for the light to change.
You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow lets you go in that direction if you are in the right lane and the road ahead is clear. This is true even if the other lights are red.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Only use your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, place your right arm on the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors because they do not show what is directly behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, you should look:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left and right for oncoming traffic or pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from the left will reach you first. Also look across the intersection to make sure the whole path is clear.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right.
The lane must turn right.
A right turn is only allowed on a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to dangerous road conditions ahead. This sign warns you of a sharp turn to the right.

questions.question: Which is a dangerous habit in a work zone?

options.text: Following another car too closely
Not paying attention to workers and equipment
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down and keep distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and moving equipment.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther away from the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: When visibility is poor due to darkness or bad weather, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react if something unexpected happens.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other car passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look at the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you start from?

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The leftmost lane.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The leftmost lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start from the far left lane.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must yield the right-of-way to them.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) in your body.

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body.

questions.question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: Stay stopped until the red lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled in, and the bus starts moving again.
